bug_semantics: During ListFonts/ListFontsWithInfo font-alias resolution, a client-controlled fonts.alias target accepted by libXfont2 can be 257-1023 bytes, while the server used 256-byte XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN-backed stack-resident tmp_pattern and current.pattern buffers. The alias paths copied resolvedlen or namelen bytes into those buffers without a preceding bound check, so a client that adds a crafted directory with SetFontPath and requests the alias can overflow the stack, crash the server, or potentially escalate privileges when the server is privileged.
flaw_origin: The earliest object in every ref of the assigned xserver clone that contains dix/dixfonts.c and include/closestr.h is ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, a 609-file all-added R6.6 baseline import. Its imported tree already contains the 256-byte definition and all relevant unchecked alias copies, and its parent contains neither path. Because an aggregate baseline import is not the smallest real source commit, it is only a history boundary and is rejected as the BIC; no decomposable original pre-import commit is present in the clone. Later libXfont-to-libXfont2 migration and memmove-to-memcpy changes preserve an already-vulnerable mechanism and are also rejected.
ai_marker: unavailable: the true smallest BIC commit object is absent from the assigned repository history. For boundary diagnosis only, git cat-file commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 shows human author/committer Kaleb Keithley, one parent, the message 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line', and no AI identity or trailer, but this rejected aggregate import cannot supply BIC-only AI evidence. The Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-6 trailer on the 2026 fix and its backports is fix-only evidence and is not attribution.
evidence: The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html states the 256-versus-1024 mismatch, the 257-1023-byte trigger range, affected X.Org Server versions before 21.1.23 and Xwayland versions before 24.1.12, and identifies bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 as the fix.

git cat-file commit bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 gives sole parent ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05. git show of its two-file patch raises XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN from 256 to 1024 and adds resolvedlen and namelen checks immediately before the alias copies, verifying that it is the direct mechanism fix rather than an aggregate or release-only change.

git log --reverse -S'memmove(tmp_pattern, resolved, resolvedlen)' ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05 -- dix/dixfonts.c and the corresponding -S'#define XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN' history first reach ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1. git show of that tree displays XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN=256, tmp_pattern[XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN], and unchecked memmove calls into tmp_pattern and current.pattern for resolvedlen/namelen.

The introducer dispute resolves in the reviewer's favor: git diff-tree --root --name-status -r ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 reports 609 added files, including dix/dixfonts.c and include/closestr.h, and its commit message is 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'. This is an aggregate import, so the primary's introducer_sha ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 is rejected under the smallest-real-BIC rule and introducer_sha is null.

The parent and parent-absence disputes also resolve in the reviewer's favor: git cat-file gives cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 as the import object's parent, and git ls-tree -r --name-only on that parent returns neither vulnerable path. That proves absence only across the rejected import boundary; it does not identify the true BIC's immediate parent. Therefore introducer_parent is null and introducer_parent_absent is false, rather than the primary's cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941/true claim.

git log --all --reverse --diff-filter=A -- dix/dixfonts.c include/closestr.h finds only the baseline import as the path-addition boundary in available refs, so there is no original commit to decompose. git show 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391 confirms a semantics-preserving memmove-to-memcpy cleanup over the already-unchecked writes, while 05a793f5b3c40747d5a92a076def7f4fb673c7e7 is a later libXfont2 API migration; neither is a BIC.

git cat-file commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 shows no AI marker, but only on the rejected import object. With no eligible earlier commit object, the required BIC-only AI check cannot be completed; the fix's Claude trailer cannot convert that gap into either AI attribution or NOT_AI.

Release-boundary checks resolve cleanly: tags xorg-server-21.1.22 and xwayland-24.1.11 contain the 256-byte definition and unchecked copies; xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12 contain the 1024-byte definition and guards. git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms backports a569eb4f36ed96a9e445ececd7e8d98c223461a0 and 93596a0b4dec958cc8f614fc25a2b68c8edc852a are respectively in the patched tags and absent from the preceding vulnerable tags, and both backport messages identify bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 as their source commit.
reasoning: The primary and reviewer agreed on the vulnerability and direct fix but disagreed on verdict, introducer_sha, introducer_parent, and parent absence. Re-running the object, pickaxe, tree, patch, and release checks confirms that ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 is the first repository snapshot containing the complete vulnerable mechanism, but also proves it is a 609-file baseline aggregate that imported the affected paths wholesale. The explicit smallest-real-BIC rule requires rejecting that import, not treating its repository parent as the vulnerable code's immediate source parent. The primary therefore over-closed the origin boundary: absence from cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 and no AI marker on the import are facts about a rejected boundary object, not valid BIC parent-absence or BIC AI evidence. The reviewer is correct that the true introducer, its direct parent, and its commit-object AI signal are unavailable in this clone. Since the fix and version gates are verified but the mandatory BIC gate cannot be closed, the gate-complete verdict is BLOCKED, not NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Commit-level history predating the R6.6 baseline import is required to identify the original smallest commit that first combined the 256-byte XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN-backed buffers with the unchecked alias-target copies, verify that commit's immediate parent lacks the mechanism, and inspect that BIC commit object for AI evidence. A trustworthy mapping from the imported snapshot to those original source commits would also close the gap; the aggregate import ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 cannot substitute for them.
